subject.title: fix #95279: Provide a trusted inbound-decoration contract so consumers can strip/dedup without forgeable text heuristics

question: Should trusted inbound-decoration state be a top-level persisted message contract or be owned inside the existing `__openclaw` metadata envelope?
rationale: This is a durable cross-reader session contract. The closed alternative proposal used `__openclaw.inboundDecoration`, while this branch uses top-level fields; selecting the permanent ownership boundary requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Use OpenClaw-owned metadata
options.body: Move the marker and bare body under the established OpenClaw metadata envelope, then update readers and compatibility tests consistently.

options.title: Approve top-level fields
options.body: Keep the additive top-level fields only with explicit maintainer approval of their persistence and consumer contract.

recommendation.title: Use OpenClaw-owned metadata
recommendation.body: Move the marker and bare body under the established OpenClaw metadata envelope, then update readers and compatibility tests consistently.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor owns the current proposal and can incorporate the selected contract direction, though an established current-main owner should make the final policy choice.
